question.text: Regulation 15 of SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012 permits Category III AIFs to employ leverage, subject to what ceiling?

answer.text: No leverage permitted (same as Cat I/II)

explanation.text: The Logic: Cat III AIFs can take leverage up to 2x of NAV per SEBI (AIF) Regulations. This is the primary structural differentiator of Cat III from Cat I/II (which have zero-leverage rule). The Trap: Option B underestimates. Option C overestimates. Option D confuses Cat I/II rule. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-D (Cat I/II) = zero leverage. XIX-B (Cat III Distributor) tests same 2x. XIX-C covers all categories. Manager's Pro-Tip: The 2x is computed on NAV INCLUDING unrealised MTM; on days of steep drawdown, the leverage ratio inflates mechanically without any new trade. Monitor two paths: trade-driven leverage and drawdown-driven leverage, and remediate drawdown-triggered breaches within T+2.
